A Common Question

Why Isn't Walking Enough?

Many older adults exercise every day—but still struggle to maintain or improve function because the body is no longer being challenged enough to adapt.

Walking, light movement, or repeating the same routine can help maintain activity, but improving strength, balance, and mobility requires progressive challenge. The body only changes when it is asked to do slightly more than what feels easy and familiar.

Progressive Challenge

Safely Pushing Further

At Tandem Strength & Balance®, we focus on safely challenging older adults at the right level so they can continue building strength, maintaining function, and staying independent longer.

Why Tandem

Strength Training That Supports Independent Living

While exercise is widely valued in younger years, it becomes even more important with age. In fact, maintaining strength is essential for preventing decline, reducing fall risk, and supporting overall health. Doctors consistently recommend exercise—but it is often not acted on until after a fall or health challenge such as diabetes, or cardiovascular and respiratory conditions.

That's where we come in.

Tandem Strength & Balance® physical therapists have been helping individuals for over 20 years regain and maintain the functional leg strength needed to live safely and independently at home. Our science-based, personalized in-home programs are designed to improve strength, stability, and confidence—so you can continue living life on your terms.

A Personalized Approach to Strength and Independence

We bring tailored strength training directly to seniors in their homes, designing programs that meet individual needs and goals. Our focus is simple: build the leg strength that supports safer movement, greater independence, and improved quality of life.

Serving the Twin Cities Metro Area

Tandem Strength & Balance® serves the entire Twin Cities metro, including Anoka, Carver, Dakota, Hennepin, Ramsey, Scott, and Washington counties.

Why It Matters

Stronger Legs, Safer Living, Greater Peace of Mind

When older adults have strong legs, families worry less—plain and simple. Strong legs mean steadier walking, better balance, and safer transfers. That means fewer falls, fewer hospital visits, and less fear in everyday movements like standing up, walking, or leaving the house.

Walking alone isn't enough. Strength is what supports safety, confidence, and independence as we age.

When legs are strong, everyone breathes easier—older adults and the people who love them.

About Tandem Strength & Balance®

Nicole – PT / Founder / Owner

Inspiring Seniors to be Stronger…Longer!

Nicole's interest in physical therapy emerged at a very young age. Her grandmother became paralyzed from the neck down under tragic circumstances. When improvements in her grandmother's condition halted, Nicole utilized a balance between tough love and encouragement to engage her grandmother to participate in her physical therapy. The plan worked and her grandmother began to improve!

After 6 years in hospitals and nursing homes serving as a physical therapist, Nicole became frustrated with the system. "Medicare physical therapy constraints stifled my passion and diminished the goals and expectations for my patients. Medicare physical therapy is an invaluable service, but it has limitations. I wanted to achieve a sustainable difference in someone's life; thus, Tandem Strength & Balance® was created!"

Nicole was driven by the scientific relationship of leg strength and mobility. Many people can't improve in the designated time allotted for by insurance companies. That does not mean that they can't get better.

It takes time to build leg strength and to make functional/balance changes. Most older adults can't or don't challenge themselves sufficiently. That is why the physical therapist is there–to explain, challenge, assist and support them in achieving how they want to live their lives.

"Tandem Strength & Balance® allows me the opportunity to be the physical therapist I have always dreamed of being. The unexpected reward is that I develop close relationships with clients and their families. I not only help people to age gracefully; I'm a part of their lives."
